name: Abishai
bio: Abishai was the son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab, a warrior under David who later became one of the fiercest commanders in David's army. When Saul pursued David with three thousand chosen men into the wilderness of Ziph, David asked who would go down with him into Saul's camp, and Abishai volunteered at once: "I'll go with you" (1 Samuel 26:6). The two slipped in by night and found Saul and his army fast asleep; Abishai told David, "God has delivered your enemy into your hands this day. Let me pin him to the ground with one thrust of the spear; I won't strike him twice." David stopped him, refusing to harm "the LORD's anointed," and instead took only Saul's spear and water jug before leaving (1 Samuel 26:7-12). This scene reveals Abishai's bold, combative nature, in contrast to David's greater restraint — a trait that would continue to define his role in David's army, with his full story unfolding through the rest of 2 Samuel.
